holidays.name: International Hat Day
holidays.description: Put on your favorite headwear and wear it with pride. Baseball cap, fedora, top hat, beanie or a wizard hat all count. It's a day to celebrate the creative, practical and sometimes ridiculous things people put on their heads.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has grown into a yearly excuse to celebrate the long history of headwear around the world.
holidays.funFact: Hats have been worn for thousands of years, and they have signaled everything from social rank to profession to simply keeping the sun out of your eyes.

holidays.name: National Parfait Day
holidays.description: A day for layering creamy, crunchy and fruity goodness in a tall glass. Build one with yogurt, granola and berries, or go for an ice cream and syrup sundae-style version. It's dessert and breakfast in one pretty tower.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands in the middle of Thanksgiving week, when a light, no-bake treat is welcome.
holidays.funFact: The word parfait is French for "perfect." The name originally described a smooth, frozen dessert made from cream, eggs and sugar.

holidays.name: Shopping Reminder Day
holidays.description: This is a friendly nudge to get your gift list in order before the holiday shopping rush. Write down who you're buying for, set a budget and scout the deals so you aren't panicking in a crowded store.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It sits just ahead of the Black Friday weekend, the busiest shopping stretch of the year in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Black Friday, the start of the holiday shopping season, always falls the day after U.S. Thanksgiving. That makes this reminder a well-timed head start.
